whispering_glades.name: Whispering Glades
lines: The Whispering Glades are gentle country by day: oak, bracken, and berries in the shade. Wolves and boar keep to the deeper wood, and the Red Fang bandits hold the ridge to the east.
Glenbrook sits at the western edge of the Glades. East of it the trees thicken, and the Old Barrow ridge is where the trouble began.
They say the glades whisper back. Stand still among the oaks at dusk and you will hear your own footsteps a moment too late.

thornwood.name: Thornwood
lines: Thornwood is the Glades' darker cousin: black pines, bramble thick as rope, and shadow wolves that do not come out of the dark until you have turned your back.
North and east of the Glades. Rangers keep a lodge there, and there is an old druid well that glows when the moon is full.
Few folk cross Thornwood after dark. The bone soldiers from the Hollow Ruins walk there, they say, and the spiders keep the east in webs.

hollow_peaks.name: Hollow Peaks
lines: The Hollow Peaks are all snow and wind. Frost bears den in the high caves and ice wisps drift over the frozen lake. Bring warm clothes and a fast friend.
At the pass there is an outpost, Frostwatch. They will sell hot soup and cold truths. Beyond that, a hermit lives in a cave who knows every herb in the mountains.
The summit shrine is older than any kingdom. Climb it if you are able, and pray you are not followed.

highmeadow.name: Highmeadow
lines: Highmeadow is the heart of the realm: farms, windmills, and the market town of Kingsford. Highwaymen prowl the road, so mind your purse.
South of the Glades. Follow the road and you will smell bread before you see the town. Kingsford is the place to hear news and spend coin.
It looks peaceful, and it mostly is, but the Bandit Lookout over the southern road keeps the Reeve awake at night.

ironhold_hills.name: Ironhold Hills
lines: Ironhold Hills are rust-red and rocky, rich in ore and poor in mercy. Brigands hold the slag heaps and golems wake in the old cuts.
The Quarry is the safest place there: stonecutters, a foreman, and a waystone. The Deepvein Mine to the east is another matter. Miners have heard things.
Somewhere in those hills is a dwarven hall, half buried in scree. Folk say the dwarves left in a hurry. They never say why.

sunscorch_dunes.name: Sunscorch Dunes
lines: The Sunscorch Dunes are the east of everything: sand, sun, and a bazaar full of striped tents. Jackals hunt in packs, scorpions grow the size of dogs, and dust wraiths follow the wind.
Carry water, always. The Oasis of Tamsin is the one safe spring for a day's walk in any direction.
Under the dunes lies a sun temple. The old sun priests are said to have left their gold and their curse in equal measure.

stormcoast.name: Stormcoast
lines: Stormcoast is sea-cliff and shingle, with a lighthouse on the point and a harbor to the south. Shore crabs, drowned sailors, and the occasional smuggler.
The harbor is where news arrives by water. Fishermen know more rumors than any priest, and tell them cheaper.
Wreck Cove has caught more ships than the rocks ever meant to. Divers say there is a pearl bed in the shallows, if you can stomach the drowned.

gloomfen.name: Gloomfen
lines: Gloomfen is a green-black mire of mist, leeches, and sinking mud. Bog lurkers wait beneath the water, and the wisps will lead you in circles if you let them.
A hermit keeps a stilt hut near the middle. A chapel stands half drowned to the south, its bell cracked and still ringing, though nobody pulls the rope.
Stick to the old boardwalks and never follow a light. Those are the two rules of the fen.

ashen_wastes.name: Ashen Wastes
lines: The Ashen Wastes are what is left when a kingdom burns. Cinder hounds, ember golems, wraiths of ash, and the Fallen Legion, who never stopped marching.
At the heart of it, an obsidian dais by a lava pool: the Ember Throne. Whoever sits there is no friend to the living.
Only the foolish and the desperate go there. A lone scholar keeps a camp in the Cinder Ruins, studying what no one wants studied.

glenbrook.name: Glenbrook
lines: Glenbrook is a quiet village of thatch and lamplight, at the west edge of the Glades. Mira keeps the herbs, Ferris the forge, and Garrick the gate.
Glenbrook's well has never frozen. The villagers count that as a blessing and do not ask why.

red_fang_camp.name: Red Fang Camp
lines: The Red Fang Camp sits on Old Barrow Ridge, east of Glenbrook. Skar's raiders hold it, and the wolves follow them like hounds.
Hunters say they can see the camp's fires from the glade road at night. Do not go in unprepared.

old_barrow.name: Old Barrow
lines: The Old Barrow is a sealed mound older than Glenbrook itself. At night it glows faintly red, which is enough to keep most folk away.
Something was dug up beneath the Old Barrow years back. Nobody will say what.

glade_pond.name: Glade Pond
lines: Glade Pond is a reed-ringed pool in the heart of the Glades. Trout in the shallows, and a pleasant place to rest.

thornwood_lodge.name: Thornwood Lodge
lines: Thornwood Lodge is a ranger post hidden in black pines. The rangers there keep the paths open and the shadow wolves honest.
If you want to know what is stalking Thornwood, ask Sylas at the lodge.

moonwell.name: The Moonwell
lines: The Moonwell is a druid shrine where a pale spring glows at night. Elowen tends it, and she does not suffer fools.
They say the water remembers every face that has ever drunk from it.

hollow_ruins.name: Hollow Ruins
lines: The Hollow Ruins are the crumbled walls of a forgotten hall in southern Thornwood. Bone soldiers walk them at night.
Treasure hunters go in. A few come out.

spider_den.name: Spider Den
lines: The Spider Den is a webbed cave mouth in Thornwood's east. Something skitters inside, and I would rather not learn what.
Rangers burn the webs from time to time. They always grow back.

old_watchtower.name: Old Watchtower
lines: The Old Watchtower leans over the eastern edge of Thornwood. It was built to see something coming. Nobody remembers what.
From the top you can see all of Thornwood, they say. And the road to the peaks.

frostwatch_outpost.name: Frostwatch Outpost
lines: Frostwatch Outpost is a palisade watching the mountain pass. Captain Ysolde keeps her people warm and her blades sharp.
If anything comes down from the Hollow Peaks, Frostwatch sees it first.

hermit_cave.name: Hermit Cave
lines: The Hermit Cave is a smoky den in the high rocks where a recluse keeps a fire burning. He does not like visitors but he knows plants.
Bring him something rare and he might talk.

frozen_lake.name: Frozen Lake
lines: The Frozen Lake is a wide sheet of black ice, southeast of Frostwatch. Ice wisps drift over it. Tread carefully.

rimefang_den.name: Rimefang Den
lines: Rimefang Den is a frost bear lair ringed with bones. The biggest bear in the peaks lives there, and the bones are not all animal.

summit_shrine.name: Summit Shrine
lines: The Summit Shrine is a ring of standing stones high in the snow. Those who climb it say the wind goes silent inside the ring.

kingsford.name: Kingsford
lines: Kingsford is the market hub of the realm: an inn, a hall, a bustling square. If you need work, news, or bread, start there.
The Reeve rules Kingsford with a fair hand and a tired voice. The inn serves the best stew in the realm.

harvest_farm.name: Harvest Farm
lines: Harvest Farm is a prosperous holding of wheat fields and a great barn, west of Kingsford. Old Maud runs it and will tell you so.
Something has been at the grain stores lately. The farmers blame the boar. The boar deny it.

old_windmill.name: Old Windmill
lines: The Old Windmill creaks on a hill east of Kingsford. Nobody has ground grain there in years. Travelers use it as a landmark.

bandit_lookout.name: Bandit Lookout
lines: The Bandit Lookout is a highwayman hideout above the southern road. The Reeve would love someone to clear it out.

ironhold_quarry.name: Ironhold Quarry
lines: Ironhold Quarry is a working stoneyard with a foreman's camp. Dorn Ashvale runs it and prizes ore above gold.
Rock golems have been wandering into the cuts of late. Dorn is not pleased.

deepvein_mine.name: Deepvein Mine
lines: Deepvein Mine is a timbered mine mouth with lanterns burning at all hours. The miners hear tapping from below that is not theirs.
Hilde Coppergate leads the crew. She would welcome someone who is not afraid of the dark.

dwarven_ruin.name: Dwarven Ruin
lines: The Dwarven Ruin is a set of ancient carved halls half buried in scree. The dwarves are gone, but the locks still hold.

slag_camp.name: Slag Camp
lines: The Slag Camp is a brigand base by the slag heaps. Hill brigands raid the quarry road from there.

iron_tarn.name: Iron Tarn
lines: The Iron Tarn is a cold, rust-colored pool in the southwest hills. The water is undrinkable. The fish are, oddly, fine.

dust_bazaar.name: Dust Bazaar
lines: The Dust Bazaar is a market of striped tents in the sand, where everything is for sale and most things are true. Zahra Qasim runs the busiest stall.
If you need something rare, a trader at the Bazaar can find it. For a price.

oasis_of_tamsin.name: Oasis of Tamsin
lines: The Oasis of Tamsin is a patch of palms and clear water in the wastes. Tamsin keeps the well, and watches the dunes for trouble.
If you cross the dunes, plan your route by the oases. They are the only mercy out there.

sun_temple.name: Sun Temple
lines: The Sun Temple is a half-buried ruin of pillars and gold leaf, in the dunes southwest of the Bazaar. The priests are gone. Their curses are not.

scorpion_pit.name: Scorpion Pit
lines: The Scorpion Pit is a sand pit crawling with chitin. Scorpions there grow big, and the chitin fetches a good price.

gull_point_lighthouse.name: Gull Point Lighthouse
lines: Gull Point Lighthouse is a white-and-red tower on a cliff, tended by Odo Saltmarsh. When the lamp goes out, ships go aground.
Odo's lamp has been guttering lately. He worries.

driftwood_harbor.name: Driftwood Harbor
lines: Driftwood Harbor is a weathered port of docks and tarred boats. The fishermen hear everything first.
Nell Tidewater runs the pearl diving here, and every sailor owes her a favour.

wreck_cove.name: Wreck Cove
lines: Wreck Cove holds the bones of a wrecked trading ship. Divers say the cargo is still down there, and so are the drowned.

tidecaller_cave.name: Tidecaller Cave
lines: Tidecaller Cave booms with the tide, northeast of the harbor. When the water is high it sings, and no sensible fisherman goes near.

smugglers_camp.name: Smugglers Camp
lines: The Smugglers' Camp is a hidden cove full of stolen crates, east of the harbor. The harbor master pretends not to know.

mossfen_hut.name: Mossfen Hut
lines: Mossfen Hut is a stilt hut above the mire, where Marrow Vane brews things that smell worse than they work. They work very well.
Marrow does not get many visitors. Bring a gift and some patience.

sunken_chapel.name: Sunken Chapel
lines: The Sunken Chapel is a half-drowned chapel in southern Gloomfen. Brother Alder tends what is left, and rings the bell when he can.
The bell rings on its own some nights. Brother Alder does not say who pulls the rope.

drowned_hollow.name: Drowned Hollow
lines: Drowned Hollow is a flooded sinkhole that bog lurkers have claimed. Divers do not come back from it.

leech_pools.name: Leech Pools
lines: The Leech Pools are still green water thick with leeches. Healers pay well for them. Do not wade in without boots.

toad_mound.name: Toad Mound
lines: The Toad Mound is a hill where giant toads gather in the wet season. Harmless unless you startle them.

cinder_ruins.name: Cinder Ruins
lines: The Cinder Ruins are the shell of an old fort in the western Wastes. A lone camp smolders there, tended by a scholar named Ignatius Vale.
A scholar living in the Wastes seems mad, but Vale has survived there for years. That says something.

ember_throne.name: Ember Throne
lines: The Ember Throne is a dais of obsidian beside a lava pool. A tyrant sits upon it, and he does not take kindly to visitors.

obsidian_spire.name: Obsidian Spire
lines: The Obsidian Spire is a black glass tower in the western Wastes. Scholars say it hums at dawn.

lava_fields.name: Lava Fields
lines: The Lava Fields are rivers of molten stone in the Wastes' northeast. The ground cracks underfoot. Do not linger.

legion_camp.name: Fallen Legion Camp
lines: The Fallen Legion Camp is where undying soldiers still guard their tents, east of the Wastes' heart. They never sleep. They never surrender.

waystone_village.name: Village Waystone
lines: The Village Waystone is one of the old waystones. Touch it and it remembers you, so you can return to it from any other attuned stone.

tips: Dire wolves hunt in packs but hit one at a time. Put your back to a tree, strike when they lunge, and do not chase when they flee.
A wolf's rush is fast but its recovery is slow. Dodge the lunge, then punish.
They fear fire and respect a steady blade. Never turn your back on one, but never charge a pack either.
Boars charge in straight lines. Sidestep and strike as they pass. Their tusks are worth good coin.
Do not get cornered by a boar. Keep room to dodge and it is an easy meal.
A boar's charge hurts, but it needs a long wind-up. Watch for the head-down stance.
Wisps drift at range and hurl bolts of cold light. Close the gap fast, or break line of sight and let them come to you.
Do not follow a wisp. It will lead you in circles, and its friends will finish you.
They are fragile. One good hit usually does it. Getting the hit is the trick.
Shadow wolves are faster than dire wolves and harder to see at night. Fight near a fire or a lit place.
They circle. Keep moving so they cannot flank, and take them down one at a time.
Bone soldiers are slow but hit hard. Keep your distance and strike after they swing.
Their shields turn aside the first blow. Strike from the side, or break the shield first.
They walk in the ruins by night. Fight them by day if you can.
Snow wolves blend into the drifts. Listen for the crunch of snow before they strike.
They fight in packs, like dire wolves, but cold-hardened and meaner. Pick the weakest first.
Frost bears are slow but strike like a landslide. Keep moving, strike from behind, and never stand your ground when you can dodge.
A frost bear's claws are big enough to cleave armor. Fight it in the open so you can circle.
If it rears up, step back. That is the slam, and it shakes the ground.
Ice wisps fire frost bolts that slow you down. Keep moving, strike hard, and do not stay within range.
They hover over the frozen lake. Draw them to land before you fight.
Highwaymen prefer an ambush. Walk the middle of the road, keep your eyes on the ridgeline, and strike first.
They run when outnumbered. Do not chase them into the woods.
Hill brigands hit hard but die easily. Fight them one at a time, and use cover against archers.
Their camps are well defended. Scout before you charge.
Rock golems are slow, tough, and hit like a landslide. Stay behind them and strike where the stone is cracked.
Avoid its stomp. After it swings, there is a long recovery. Hit then, and step away.
Jackals hunt in packs and strike from the flank. Use a narrow dune to keep them in front of you.
They are fast but weak. One solid hit usually scatters them.
Scorpions strike with their tail after a quick feint. Dodge sideways and attack the soft underside.
Their chitin is tough from the front. Circle to the side.
Dust wraiths come on the wind and vanish when struck. Keep moving. They only hit what stands still.
They hate light. A torch or campfire holds them at bay.
Shore crabs pinch hard and walk sideways, which makes them hard to hit. Strike when they raise their claws.
Easy meat for a patient hunter. They are slow to turn.
Drowned sailors rise from the surf at night. They are slow, wet, and angry. Keep to dry land and fire.
Their blows are heavy, but they do not dodge. Strike and step back.
Bog lurkers wait submerged and lunge when you pass. Keep to the boardwalks and watch for ripples.
After a lurker lunges it is exposed. Hit it then, and back away before it submerges.
Bog boars are mean cousins of the forest kind. Same charge, same rhythm, but more mud and worse manners.
Cinder hounds run hot and leave burning trails. Fight them on bare stone, away from anything flammable.
They bark before they lunge. That is your warning. Dodge.
Ember golems throw fire when wounded. Close in fast, then retreat from the burst.
Their cores are worth a fortune. Break the shell first.
Ash wraiths fade in and out. Strike when they solidify to attack, not before.
They drain warmth and spirit. Do not stand in their cloud.
Ashen knights are the Legion's finest. Slow, armored, and relentless. Dodge the overhead strikes, and hit during recovery.
Wearing one down takes patience. Do not let them pin you.
Red Fang bandits fight with axes and bad tempers. Block or dodge, strike during recovery, and do not let them surround you.
They carry insignia worth coin to the guard. Take them in small groups.
Archers keep their range. Close fast, or break line of sight and ambush them around a corner.
They flee when you get close. Do not follow into the open.
Skar fights like a man possessed, because he is. Wait for his big swing, dodge, and strike hard. Bring healing.
His wolves come when he howls. Kill them or stay out of their path.
